meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas. doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.mechanism: Renal cancers frequently carry lesions that leave mTORC1 constitutively active - which is why this tissue responds to mTOR inhibitors at all, and why an exceptional responder could be traced to TSC1 loss.
data.mechanism_beginner: Many kidney cancers carry mutations that leave mTORC1 stuck "on" – that's why this cancer type responds to mTOR-blocking drugs at all, though it doesn't prove mTORC1 causes the cancer.
data.boundary: Correlative plus one n-of-1 genomic case (IYE2012); not a demonstration that mTORC1 activation initiates RCC.
data.note: Replaces TUMOR-RCC, which asserted 'Tumor growth activates RCC' - a category error, since RCC is an instance of tumour growth, not a downstream target.
